newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa truth commission may sit in Botswana.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa truth commission may sit in Botswana.

text.p: South Africa's search for the truth about crimes under apartheid could soon be taken across the border to neighbouring Botswana.

The Department of Foreign Affairs said on Wednesday South Africa was awaiting Botswana's permission to allow the truth body to hold a session there to probe cross-border raids by the apartheid-era South African Defence Force hunting African National Congress (ANC) activists.

President Nelson Mandela set up the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to heal the wounds of apartheid by exposing the dirty tricks and suffering of all sides during the struggle between liberation movements and the white minority government.
Botswana's weekly Gazette newspaper reported on Wednesday that Botswana's cabinet had turned down the request at a meeting last week and said a statement would be issued later.

But South African High Commissioner to Botswana, Oupa Mokou, said he had not been informed of the decision. "I would not say that, I have not been informed of any decision," he said reacting to the newspaper report.
Mokou said there were still legal and financial issues to be discussed on the holding of such a meeting.
"I think the Botswana government is bound to agree to the commission sitting in Gaborone, but it still wants the answers to certain questions," he said.
"We cannot expect Botswana to allow the commission to come until its government has full information about what is likely to happen," he added.
